question:
Create a new KiCad project named b37 in the project directory and draw its schematic for the following request.

Build one reversible half of a wireless split keyboard with a nice!nano module, eighteen Choc hot-swap keys, one diode per key, a battery switch, reset button and nice!view display. Use the supplied dumta module/display symbols and reversible footprints.
Firmware matrix: rows 0-3 use nice!nano D4, D5, D6, D7; columns 0-4 use D21, D20, D19, D18, D15. Rows 0-2 have five keys each, numbered SW1-SW15 in row order; row 3 has SW16-SW18 in columns 2, 3, 4. Switches connect columns to diode anodes, with cathodes on the row lines. The nice!view header is MOSI/D2, SCK/D3, VCC, GND, CS/D1. Battery negative is GND; battery positive reaches the module's BATTERY+ through the SPDT switch, using one throw for on and leaving the other open. Reset shorts RESET to GND. Charging and regulation are already on the controller module.
Local dependencies: Use the project-local symbol library (dumta.kicad_sym) and footprint library (dumta.pretty) in lib/ under the project directory; use standard KiCad libraries for everything else.
